description_good_justification: The README opens with what the project is and does: an MCP server that gives AI assistants access to Thunderbird mail, filters, contacts and calendars, with a review window before anything is sent. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: Obtain: README "Setup" (GitHub releases, or git clone). Feedback: CONTRIBUTING "Reporting bugs and requesting features" (GitHub issues). Contribute: CONTRIBUTING (pull requests, ground rules, local checks). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: Contributions are GitHub pull requests; CONTRIBUTING describes the process, the ground rules and the local checks. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING "Ground rules": no vulnerability details in public before a fix, synthetic data only, tests with every change, pinned dependencies, small privileged surface. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ground-rules
floss_license_justification: MIT license (original copyright Tomasz Kasperczyk, plus the Commonpost contributors); the embedded Mozilla HTTP server is MPL-2.0 (THIRD-PARTY.md). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the root of the repository, also shipped inside the XPI. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: README: purpose, how it works, the tools, setup, security model, troubleshooting, development. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the set of MCP tools, documented tool by tool in the README ("What you can do") and described to clients through tools/list. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/README.md#what-you-can-do
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository and downloads are on GitHub, over HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, URL-addressable, open to new participants, no proprietary client required. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/issues
english_justification: All documentation, code, issues and pull requests are in English.
maintained_justification: Maintained: commits, CI on every change, weekly Dependabot, CodeQL and Scorecard runs. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/commits/main
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: All commits are public, interim ones included; changes to main go through pull requests (enforced by a repository ruleset), e.g. #1 to #4 after v0.8.0. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/pulls?q=is%3Apr
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version number and tag (vX.Y.Z), identical in package.json, the manifest and the release asset name. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/releases
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning (X.Y.Z); the release workflow refuses a tag that differs from package.json and the manifest.
version_tags_justification: Each release is a git tag vX.Y.Z on main with a GitHub release. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md, and each GitHub release carries the section of CHANGELOG.md for its version. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability with a CVE yet; when one does, its changelog entry names the CVE.
report_process_justification: Bug reports and feature requests: GitHub issues, as described in CONTRIBUTING. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs-and-requesting-features
report_responses_justification: We aim to acknowledge every bug report within 14 days (CONTRIBUTING).
enhancement_responses_justification: We aim to acknowledge enhancement requests within 14 days, like bug reports (CONTRIBUTING).
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are a public, searchable archive. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md explains how to report vulnerabilities (privately through GitHub, never in a public issue), the response targets (acknowledgement within 72 hours, triage within 7 days) and the scope. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/security/policy
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, as SECURITY.md explains. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months.
build_justification: `node scripts/build-xpi-reproducible.cjs` builds the XPI from the committed tree (documented in README and CONTRIBUTING; run by the release workflow); `scripts/build.sh` is the quick development build.
build_common_tools_justification: Node.js and git; no proprietary tool. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/scripts/build-xpi-reproducible.cjs
test_justification: Automated tests with the Node.js test runner (`npm test`), including property-based tests with fast-check, run in CI on every pull request and push. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/actions
test_invocation_justification: Standard command `npm test` (documented in CONTRIBUTING "Working locally").
test_most_justification: The unit tests and the end-to-end lab cover 82.6% of the statements (Coverage workflow, scripts/coverage): the tool schemas, the bridge, authentication, attachments, filters and the build, and every tool in a real Thunderbird.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every pull request and push to main. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/actions
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes shipped with tests (for example test/start-state.test.cjs, test/build-reproducible.test.cjs, test/properties.test.js).
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING rule 3 asks to say in the pull request which tests were added.
warnings_justification: ESLint (`npm run lint`) runs in CI; CodeQL and zizmor analyse code and workflows on every change.
warnings_fixed_justification: ESLint runs in CI on every pull request and push to main with no error and no warning: the warnings inherited from upstream were fixed, and the one false positive (the Experiment API entry point that Thunderbird reads by name) is marked in the source. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/actions
warnings_strict_justification: The ESLint configuration is conservative on purpose (bug detection over style).
know_secure_design_justification: The lead maintainer applies secure design principles in this project: least privilege for the add-on and its bridge, input validation at the MCP boundary, a human review window before anything is sent, safe defaults (automatic forwarding blocked by default) and isolation of untrusted code during reviews.
know_common_errors_justification: The lead maintainer knows the common vulnerability classes of this kind of software (injection, including mail header injection, path traversal, unsafe HTML handling, secrets in logs, over-broad permissions) and how to counter them; see the review notes in pull requests and the property and stress tests.
crypto_published_justification: No cryptography of our own: TLS through GitHub, SHA-256 hashes in the update manifest, Sigstore build provenance, and the browser-grade nsIRandomGenerator for tokens.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography is delegated to Thunderbird (nsIRandomGenerator, TLS) and to GitHub (attestations); the project implements none itself.
crypto_floss_justification: Thunderbird/Gecko (MPL), Sigstore (Apache-2.0) and GitHub Actions attestation tooling.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project generates no cryptographic keys for users; the auth token is 256 bits of CSPRNG output.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm or mode is used (SHA-256, CSPRNG tokens, timing-safe comparison).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 is used for any security purpose.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project implements no key agreement protocol.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project stores no user passwords; the local bearer token is a random secret, not a password.
crypto_random_justification: The auth token comes from nsIRandomGenerator (Thunderbird's cryptographically secure generator), 32 bytes, hex-encoded. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/extension/mcp_server/api.js
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases and the update manifest are delivered over HTTPS (GitHub, GitHub Pages); the manifest carries the sha256 of each release, and Thunderbird checks it.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The update manifest is served over HTTPS and its update_hash is verified by Thunderbird; the hash is published nowhere over plain HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity that have been publicly known for more than 60 days.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Confirmed vulnerabilities are fixed in a patch release as soon as the fix is verified, with coordinated disclosure (SECURITY.md). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/security/policy
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The public repository contains no valid private credentials; GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub code scanning default setup, JavaScript), zizmor (pedantic, GitHub Actions workflows) and ESLint run on every pull request and push to main. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/actions
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL security queries and zizmor look for common vulnerabilities (injection, unpinned actions, excessive permissions).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The four CodeQL alerts raised by the first scan were triaged and fixed the next day in pull request #4; no static analysis alert is open. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/pull/4
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main (CodeQL and Scorecard also run weekly).
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based tests (fast-check) run in CI and check the strict Base64 validator and the tool argument validator against generated input (test/properties.test.js).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The property tests assert the validators' contracts on generated input.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The dynamic analysis (property-based tests with fast-check and the Thunderbird smoke tests in CI) has no open finding; confirmed security issues from any source are fixed in a patch release with coordinated disclosure (SECURITY.md). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/actions
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md: roles, how decisions are made, releases through a protected environment. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md 'Roles' lists the maintainer, contributors and upstream with what each can do. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
bus_factor_justification: One maintainer today; GOVERNANCE.md explains how a second one joins.
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/architecture.md: components, data flow, build and release. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
documentation_security_justification: What the software protects and does not: docs/assurance-case.md (threat model, known limits) and SECURITY.md (scope). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: README 'Quick install (about 3 minutes)' gets a user from download to a first tool call. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: Docs change in the same pull request as the behaviour (README tool table, CHANGELOG [Unreleased]); each release turns [Unreleased] into the release notes.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page links this badge. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/README.md
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub and GitHub Pages; the project itself stores no passwords.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Installed add-ons update through the update manifest (updates.json on GitHub Pages); CHANGELOG says what breaks and what to do; the add-on warns about an outdated bridge.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: SECURITY.md 'Recognition': reporters are credited in the release notes and advisories unless they ask not to be. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md: private vulnerability reporting, 72 h acknowledgement, 7-day triage, patch release, coordinated disclosure, published GitHub advisories. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
coding_standards_justification: ESLint configuration (eslint.config.mjs) is the coding standard; CONTRIBUTING asks to keep privileged code in two files. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/eslint.config.mjs
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The Lint check (eslint .) is required to merge into main.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native code is compiled: the add-on and the bridge are plain JavaScript.
build_non_recursive_justification: The build is a single Node script per artifact (scripts/build-xpi-reproducible.cjs, scripts/build-mcpb-reproducible.cjs); no recursive build.
build_repeatable_justification: Builds are reproducible byte for byte from a tag (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, entries sorted by path with a fixed time); the release job rebuilds and refuses any difference. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/RELEASING.md
installation_common_justification: The XPI installs through Thunderbird's add-on manager (Install Add-on From File) and updates itself; the bridge ships as a Claude Desktop bundle (.mcpb) and a Claude Code plugin.
installation_standard_variables_justific: No installer writes to system locations: Thunderbird installs the add-on in the user profile.
installation_development_quick_justifica: CONTRIBUTING 'Working locally': npm ci --ignore-scripts, npm test, npm run lint, one build command. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
external_dependencies_justification: The add-on and the bridge have no third-party runtime dependencies (the bridge uses only Node built-ins); development dependencies are listed in package.json and pinned in package-lock.json; the vendored httpd.sys.mjs is listed in THIRD-PARTY.md.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version and security updates (npm, GitHub Actions) and Dependabot alerts are enabled.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: npm dependencies come from the lockfile and are updated by Dependabot; the one vendored file (httpd.sys.mjs) names its upstream source in THIRD-PARTY.md.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every pull request and push runs unit tests (Node 22 and 24), Thunderbird compatibility checks and the end-to-end lab in a real Thunderbird (commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab).
regression_tests_added50_justification: 84 of the 99 fix commits since 2026-05-03 add or change a test (CONTRIBUTING rule 3 asks for a failing test with each fix).
test_statement_coverage80_justification: 82.6% of the statements of the project's own code (api.js, options.js, background.js, mcp-bridge.cjs, scripts/) on 2026-11-04: the unit tests under Node's V8 coverage plus the public lab scenarios run in a real Thunderbird on an instrumented add-on. The Coverage workflow measures it on main and every week and fails below 80%. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/actions/workflows/coverage.yml
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING rule 3: new functionality comes with a test in the same pull request. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/assurance-case.md lists the secure design principles applied, with where each is implemented. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The only credential is the token between bridge and add-on, generated at random at each start; no credential is compiled in.
signed_releases_justification: Each release carries Sigstore build-provenance attestations (.sigstore.json) and the same statements as .intoto.jsonl; users verify them with gh attestation verify (RELEASING.md). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/RELEASING.md
input_validation_justification: Every tool argument is checked against its schema and in its handler (types, sizes, paths, account restrictions) before use; see docs/assurance-case.md. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md: threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles and the common weaknesses countered, with known limits. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
